reason: u1 is kept unchanged: it directly implements the Goal's requirement to broaden non-desklamp localization beyond closed cabinets/drawers to surfaces and appliances, and it is executable and compatible with the Parent. Current evidence supports the direction (in P1 the Actor exhausted and re-walked cabinets/drawers and only found the requested box after reaching coffeetable 1 at P1:36; the target in P3 was never located while cycling through cabinets), and memory shows the same benefit (bread located on the diningtable in M6; newspaper/candle/saltshaker instances on coffeetable/countertop/cabinet in M9). No definite defect, exclusion of a legal option, or contradicted guarantee appears in u1, and its multi-target completion clause remains relevant to P6, so no correction is warranted. u2, by contrast, needs narrowing. Its first clause makes an absolute prohibition keyed to 'a receptacle you have already confirmed empty' and 'your recent observation/action history', but the Actor only receives the last two pre-action observations and cannot reliably determine the full prior set of confirmed-empty receptacles; this is a global condition projected onto information the Actor does not actually have. Memory also shows this same anti-cycling wording was repeatedly not followed and failed to break cycling (M3 found the 'do not immediately revisit' clause unreliable; M6 records the anti-cycling/step-budget rewrite being unreliable, with the Candidate choosing an unavailable move to cabinet 3, falling back to a no-op, and then examining that already-empty location; M9 records continuing to revisit already-open empty shelves/drawers). I therefore keep the necessary behavior (avoid immediate re-walks and complete one inspection of untested receptacles) but re-anchor the trigger to the current and previous observation, condition the prohibition on another untried candidate remaining (so the Actor is not pushed into unavailable moves), and extend the stuck-search break action to include uninspected unopened containers rather than only surfaces or appliances, so it does not exclude the Parent's closed-container search. This is a scope/trigger correction supported by the cited history; it is not evidence that broader search itself is harmful, and the narrowed wording remains an untested hypothesis whose effect must be observed by the checks.

--- a/SKILL.md
+++ b/SKILL.md
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
-- After inspecting a receptacle that visibly lacks the exact target, do not re-open or re-walk a receptacle you have already confirmed empty; next travel to a receptacle that does not appear in your recent observation/action history and whose contents you have not yet seen.
-- Do not cycle back and forth among the same small set of receptacles; before making any second pass over a container cluster, complete one inspection of the remaining untested receptacle types or instances.
-- Treat a run of steps that only revisits already-open, empty containers as a stuck-search signal: break the pattern by moving to an uninspected surface or appliance instead of repeating the loop.
+- After inspecting a receptacle that visibly lacks the exact target, do not re-open, re-examine, or re-walk that same receptacle when another candidate remains; choose a next destination other than the receptacle you just left whose contents you have not yet seen, using the current and previous observations rather than assuming you remember every receptacle visited.
+- Do not cycle back and forth among the same small set of receptacles; before making any second pass over a container cluster, complete one inspection of the remaining untested receptacle types or instances.
+- If the current and previous observation both show you at an already-open receptacle that lacks the exact target, treat that as a stuck-search signal: move to a different untried receptacle, including an uninspected unopened drawer or cabinet, an uninspected surface, or an uninspected appliance, instead of re-examining a known-empty location or repeating the loop.

adjustments.reason: Narrow u2's trigger. The absolute prohibition tied to 'a receptacle you have already confirmed empty' presupposes complete historical state the Actor cannot access with only the last two pre-action observations, and this anti-cycling formulation was repeatedly ineffective (M3, M6, M9), including the observed pattern of choosing an unavailable move and then examining an already-empty location (M6). The current runs confirm the same re-walking of already-open empty locations (P1:15 go to open empty cabinet 1; P3:48 go to open empty cabinet 1; P6:26 go to open empty drawer 1, with P3 and P6 ending at the step limit). The rewrite keeps the necessary behavior (no immediate re-walk when an alternative exists; complete one inspection of untested receptacles) but uses an Actor-visible local trigger, conditions on another candidate being available to avoid driving unavailable/fallback actions, adds a prohibition on re-examining known-empty locations, and widens the break-the-loop action to include uninspected unopened containers so it does not conflict with the Parent's closed-container search. This is a trigger/scope correction; it does not establish that the narrowed wording works, which the retained checks must observe. u1 is unchanged because its broadening requirement is goal-directed and supported by P1:36 and M6/M9.
